objective_for_doctor: Assess and diagnose the patient presenting with hypopigmented skin patches.

turns.content: Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—let’s start with your skin patches: when did they first appear, and are they getting bigger over time? Patient: They started a few months ago and slowly got larger.
Patient: They began a few months ago on my hands and face, and yes—they’ve been gradually getting larger. I don’t have any itching, pain, or burning where the patches are.

Doctor: Thanks—2 quick questions: are the patches completely lighter than your surrounding skin (well-demarcated) or just “faded,” and have you noticed any changes in hair/eyebrows/eyelashes in those areas or new numbness? Doctor: Also, can you tell me if you’ve had recent sun exposure or any new medicines/illness in the months before they started?

Patient: They’re clearly lighter and pretty well-defined, not just faded. I haven’t noticed any changes in my hair, eyebrows, or eyelashes there, and no numbness. I’ve had normal sun exposure at university, but no major burns, and I didn’t start any new medicines or have any recent illnesses around when they began.

Doctor: Any family history of similar light patches, and are the patches made worse by sun or do they stay the same color over time? Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Wood_Lamp_Examination (to check for depigmentation pattern).

RESULTS: Temperature 36.8°C (98.2°F); Blood pressure 115/70 mmHg; Heart rate 72 bpm; Respiratory rate 14 breaths/min. Skin exam: multiple well-demarcated hypopigmented patches on the backs of the hands, face, and neck with no erythema, scaling, or atrophy; normal skin texture; no tenderness or palpable masses. Histopathology (skin biopsy): absence of melanocytes in the epidermis. Wood’s lamp examination: NORMAL READINGS (not provided in available data).

Doctor: With well-demarcated hypopigmented patches and biopsy showing absent melanocytes in the epidermis, this pattern is most consistent with vitiligo rather than pityriasis versicolor or post-inflammatory hypopigmentation. Doctor: DIAGNOSIS READY: Vitiligo
